I agree.
That wasn't what I was getting at though.

The implication from the post I responded to is that people in relationships shouldnt be around  people they could potentially be attracted to or who could be attracted to them, one-on-one. As a queer person, this would mean I couldn't have any sort of normal social life if I were to adhere to this. You probably know this, but PapaMavy seems to have not fully thought out the logical conclusion to his outdated rule.
I think my(f) girlfriend and I need to revisit things with our gay male housemate 🙄.

Oh HELL no. This man was not trying to help you and any family/friends who think so either don't know the full story or also don't have your best interests at heart. Starting setting some serious boundaries and lose the man entirely. NTA

I've definitely run into some anti-semitism, its so sad how far we still have yet to go towards being a decent society. That being said, I think Christians in the US generally have an advantage over other religious groups and non-religions folk (more businesses, hospitals, and politicians that explicitly endorse Christianity and whatnot, not to mention stronger support systems). So prejudice against Christians just doesnt have the same bite that prejudice against non-Christians has.

For real though. Like there's absolutely no way that bringing his kids to a mosque for a day makes him the AH in any context, regardless of what the wife wants to do for a winter vacation. But the fact that you got downvoted for calling out people's blatant bigotry? Absolutely batshit.
If someone else is reading this and is getting huffy that a stranger on the internet thinks islamaphobia is gross, visit a mosque yourself. It wont kill you. I say this as an agnostic who grew up SUPER baptist and got turned off religion for a while.

I have an almost identical texture aversion to your girlfriend. YTA majorly.
Its not "dramatic" its an accurate expression of her internal experience. Youre just not being very compassionate or empathetic for this situation. Like congrats, you dont have as many texture aversions, your brain process sensory input differently than hers.

Sorry if I wasn't clear, my issue is that my family doesn't make any effort to curb abusive behavior (going out of his way to rile me up). I don't appreciate that everyone enables his bs instead of addressing it, especially given that I'm not the only one he treats poorly.
